## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pañcavagga* ("Fivefold Section") constitutes the twenty-first chapter of the *Parivāra*, the procedural and analytical manual forming the final major division of the Pali *Vinayapiṭaka* [SuttaCentral]. The text analyzes Vinaya matters arranged under five principal themes: the legal validity of formal monastic transactions (*kamma*), the foundational reasons for the promulgation of the Vinaya, the categories of legal procedures entailed, the specific rationales for these procedures, and a ninefold classification scheme [SuttaCentral]. An English translation by Bhikkhu Brahmali is available on SuttaCentral under the descriptive title *Legal procedures, why the Monastic Law, resolution of legal issues* [SuttaCentral].

The chapter displays extensive internal text reuse across the Pali canon and Vinaya commentaries, with DharmaNexus registering 1,922 matching passages across 58 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Substantial textual overlap occurs with the *Campeyyakkhandhaka* (Kd 9) of the Khandhakas (such as §2.6–2.17 matching Kd 9 §6.5.3–6.5.13), as well as internal *Parivāra* parallels with the *Katthapaññattivāra* (Pvr 1.1) and *Ekuttarikanaya* (Pvr 7) [DharmaNexus]. It also shares passages with the Sutta Piṭaka, particularly the *Dukanipāta* of the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (§29.1–31.5 matching AN 2.281–309, paralleling SuttaCentral's cross-reference to AN 2.280) and the *Dasakanipāta* (AN 10) [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. Later commentarial treatises that cite or share large portions of the text include the *Vinayasaṅgaha-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Parivāra-aṭṭhakathā*, and the *Vinayavinicchaya-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus]. Across non-Pali traditions, DharmaNexus automatically aligns segments of the text with Tibetan versions of the *Vinayavastu* (D0001 / D0001-3) and *Vinayasūtravṛtti* (D4122), as well as Sanskrit *Prātimokṣasūtra* fragments [DharmaNexus].

Secondary literature passages retrieved under the name *pañcavagga* do not discuss this specific *Parivāra* text, referring instead to the monastic quorum of five monks (*pañcavaggasaṅgha*) or homonymous section titles in other collections.
